notes.1: Many candidates appreciated that the release of energy from nutrient molecules is respiration. Some candidates incorrectly selected nutrition.
notes.2: Many candidates correctly selected the monocotyledon, option D . Monocotyledons can be identified because their flower parts are in multiples of three. Cambridge International General Certificate of Secondary Education 0610 Biology June 2022
notes.7: Few candidates appreciated that both starch and glycogen are made of glucose molecules.
notes.15: Identifying both the part of the plant shown (the root) and the tissue labelled H (the phloem) proved difficult for most candidates.
notes.18: Many candidates correctly identified component X as fibrinogen. Some incorrectly selected fibrin. This shows some uncertainty about which substance is converted into the other.
notes.20: Many candidates were able to deduce the correct answer as option C . Some candidates though were uncertain whether the internal and external intercostal muscles contract or relax at the start of inspiration.
notes.22: It was well understood that aerobic respiration breaks down lactic acid in the liver. Some candidates incorrectly believed that the lactic acid is broken down in the muscles.
notes.25: While many candidates gave the correct response, some candidates incorrectly believed that glucagon is produced by the liver.
notes.26: Many candidates understood that auxin becomes concentrated in the lower part of the shoot and the shoot grows towards the light. Some candidates incorrectly believed that auxin becomes concentrated in the upper part of the shoot.
notes.27: Many candidates understood that an adaptive feature of sperm is the presence of enzymes in the acrosome. Some candidates incorrectly believed that sperm cells have large stores of energy.
notes.30: Many candidates understood that cells produced by meiosis would contain half the number of chromosomes (12). Some candidates incorrectly believed that the cells would contain twice the number of chromosomes (48).
notes.32: Candidates needed to carefully assess which of the features would be an adaptation for hydrophytes. Large air spaces inside the leaves would allow the leaves to float on the surface of the water.
notes.37: Only a minority of candidates understood that all kingdoms share the same genetic code. Cambridge International General Certificate of Secondary Education 0610 Biology June 2022
